content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: SEV=P1 — Traffic blackholing from dedicated router fallback loop (eu-west-1). Detected 502 spikes and elevated error rates for customers on Dedicated pools. Pager: oncall-eng@redwood.

Alex P: acknowledged. I'm on-call and see the dashboards. Errors jump at 23:33 UTC, routing fallback thrash between variant-a and variant-b every ~20s.

Maria Sanchez: saw the same. Metric that drove router decisions (route_available_instances) flipped to 0 for pool-dedicated-eu-3 while container counts in cluster were stable. Looks like a telemetry swap at the router-proxy level.

Jordan T: digging logs now. Query I ran: ```promql
sum by(pool) (rate(router_fallback_events_total{pool=~"dedicated-eu.*"}[1m]))
```
shows repeated fallback increments aligned with the 502 spikes.

Leah K: Customer impact: three customers on Dedicated had request error rates >15% for 10-12 minutes. Tickets already opened: TKT-4521, TKT-4523. Notified customer success.

Alex P: initial mitigation plan: 1) throttle fallback policy to stop oscillation (set fallback.window_s=120) 2) temporarily pin routing to variant-a for affected pools 3) scale up pool count as safety. Executing step 1 now.

Maria Sanchez: step 1 done — updated policy via console to `fallback.window_s=120` and `fallback.backoff=exponential(30s, 5)` — watch metrics.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: applied config change to routes/fallback-policy/overrides for dedicated-eu-3 by Alex P @ 23:37 UTC.

Jordan T: I see the oscillation slow but not stop. There's a second problem: the autoscaler reported `available_instances=0` due to a label mismatch after a recent agent rollout; router treats pool as drained. Checking autoscaler logs. Relevant excerpt: ```
2026-11-09T23:31:12Z autoscaler INFO pool=dedicated-eu-3 available=0 label=instance.group=dedicated-eu-b
2026-11-09T23:31:12Z kube-proxy WARN inconsistent labels: expected instance.group=dedicated-eu-3
```

Maria Sanchez: that lines up. Router relies on the 'available' signal for routing weight. If autoscaler swapped label names, router thinks pool has zero capacity and falls back to variant-b. When variant-b is overloaded, it fails and router flips back — loop.

Alex P: short-term mitigation: 1) re-route by override (pin) 2) bump pool capacity (manual scale) 3) open a rollback for the agent rollout that changed labels. I'm doing manual scale to +3 instances now.

Leah K: scaling command executed: `infractl pool scale --pool dedicated-eu-3 --replicas 6` — manual scaling in progress.

ops-bot: infra-bot: scaling started for dedicated-eu-3 by Alex P.

Jordan T: I pushed a targeted iptables rule on routers to prefer primary variant for tenant routes affected. This is a bandaid but reduces customer error rate quickly.

Maria Sanchez: autoscaler team alert: @eng-ml please confirm if agent rollout 2026-11-09T23:25 mutated label names.

eng-oncall: oncall-ml: Confirmed — the agent change introduced a legacy label mapping bug. Rolling back to agent v2.13.1 recommended.

Alex P: rolling back agent on a subset of autoscaler nodes (canary) to v2.13.1 now. Will monitor label correctness.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollback started for autoscaler-agent on nodes set auto-scale-group-a (3 nodes).

Maria Sanchez: after manual scale and routing override, customer errors drop to <2% within 3 minutes, and 502s subside. Metrics: `router_5xx_rate` went from 18% to 1.8% for affected pools.

Jordan T: still seeing a few stragglers where fallback policy didn't honor override due to cache TTL. Flushing router config cache with: `curl -XPOST http://router-admin/flush-cache?pool=dedicated-eu-3` fixed remaining routes.

Alex P: summary for pager: cause = agent rollout mutated autoscaler labels -> autoscaler reported 0 available_instances -> router fallback policy kicked in -> variant swap overloaded fallback variant causing 502s -> repeated swaps created blackhole.

Leah K: customer impact summary to include: 3 Dedicated customers, spikes for ~12 minutes, ~5k failed requests total, no data exfiltration. CS notified, SLAs may need make-good.

eng-oncall: oncall-ml: rollback completed on canary. Verified label metrics back to normal on canary nodes. Scheduling full rollback; ETA 18 minutes.

Maria Sanchez: full rollback in progress. Monitoring `route_available_instances` and `router_fallback_events_total`.

ops-bot: infra-bot: full rollback complete @ 23:58 UTC. Autoscaler labels restored.

Alex P: removing temporary routing override and restoring fallback.window_s to previous safe defaults. Doing gradual restore: `fallback.window_s=30` and `backoff=exponential(10s,3)`

Maria Sanchez: restored fallback config. Watching for recurrence. No more flips observed for 15 minutes.

Jordan T: filed an action item: add a metric-based sanity check to prevent label-swapped agent versions from being considered healthy by autoscaler. Filed as ENG-OPS-742.

Alex P: on-call handoff to night team at 00:15 UTC. Leaving notes: root cause, rollback, commands used, customer impact, tickets.

Leah K: copy. I'll take night handoff. Please post a short incident note in #postmortems with timeline and RCA when we've fully recovered.

Alex P: will do. Thanks all.

Maria Sanchez: quick follow-up: add alert that watches for routing thrash: if fallback events > 10/min for same pool -> auto-mute fallback and page SRE. Filed as ENG-ALERT-319.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Pager cleared at 00:20 UTC.

eng-oncall: closure checklist: create postmortem, customer comms draft, automation to prevent future label-rollouts.

Alex P: closing thread for now. Postmortem draft will be uploaded to #postmortems by EOD.

ops-bot: Note: small follow-up job scheduled to add label compatibility tests in rollout pipeline.
